files.README.md:
# tracked-paths

parse_paths(output) receives the already decoded UTF-8 text of Git ls-files -z output, with no other ls-files flags enabled. Input is empty or consists of nonempty paths, each terminated by NUL. Return a Python list of the paths in order, preserving every filename character, including spaces, newlines, tabs, quotes and backslashes. Follow the documented -z quoting and termination rules; do not run git.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/git/git/v2.46.0/Documentation/git-ls-files.txt
Run: `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests`. Keep the public interface and original tests. Standard library/built-ins only; no network or git in application code. Runtime artifacts belong in the system temporary directory.
files.tests/test_behavior.py:
import unittest
from tracked_paths import parse_paths

class TrackedPaths(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_nul_terminated_verbatim_paths(self):
        rows = [
            ('', []),
            ('src/oak.py\0docs/leaf.md\0', ['src/oak.py', 'docs/leaf.md']),
            (' notes \0line\nbreak.txt\0tab\tname\0', [' notes ', 'line\nbreak.txt', 'tab\tname']),
            ('"quoted".txt\0a\\b.txt\0木.txt\0', ['"quoted".txt', 'a\\b.txt', '木.txt']),
            ('same\0same\0', ['same', 'same']),
            (' \0', [' ']),
        ]
        for output, expected in rows:
            with self.subTest(output=output):
                self.assertEqual(parse_paths(output), expected)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()
